step: NEXT-PLAN.md § 4 — the baseline, made honest, gated and visible

model.name: xgboost
model.feature_note: every column is a shift or a backward window of the 7-gauge chain; proven causal against a truncated series on every run

windows.role: in-sample: the window the model was fitted on, shown for contrast only
the published holdout: contains the 2016 Memorial Day flood and Harvey
out of sample, after the holdout — never used to choose anything
out of sample, the most recent complete years in the caches

comparison.summary: beats persistence on 12/15 out-of-sample window-horizons; loses on 3 — all of them at +5 d and +7 d
comparison.losses_note: beyond +3 days this model is not better than assuming today's stage, on every window after the holdout — it is shipped as a cross-check on the ensemble's error, never as the answer

limits: the published holdout is 2016-17 and it is the window with the largest errors; the later windows are easier, so a single-window score flatters the model
in-sample RMSE is two orders of magnitude below the holdout — the comparison that matters is against persistence, not against zero error
the deterministic seed fixes the fit but not the library: xgboost's version is recorded here, and the golden regression is what notices a change
the two explicit lag columns duplicate existing shifts; kept so the published benchmark stays comparable
no antecedent precipitation, because MRMS QPE starts in 2014 and the training matrix starts 2013-08 at San Felipe — a Phase 2 blocker, not a modelling choice
thresholds at 45 and 50 ft are exceeded in very few windows, so their CSI is reported with the counts it came from and is not a stable rate

provenance.forecast_error_consumer: pipeline/derive/ensemble.py reads the holdout RMSE knots of this benchmark to perturb forecast points
provenance.gauge_chain: pipeline/analyze/travel_time.py (the lags the chain is built on)
